title: Madame Guil
summary: A justicar and the archons sworn to that office.

claims.text: Madame Guil was born a French peasant and knew only hunger in youth.
A justicar usually keeps 15 to 20 archons and countless informants, and Guil's chief archons are all blood bound to the justicar.
Guil has spent a century hunting anarchs to silence rumours of sympathy for them, and the strain has left Guil close to madness.

title: Hafsa, the Watcher
summary: An Assamite raised for the clan who now serves Madame Guil.

claims.text: The Assamites sometimes take children at birth and raise them in the clan fortress for the Embrace; Hafsa was raised this way, taught only to fight, hunt and hide.
Embraced, Hafsa learned hatred and did not stay loyal to the clan, and now serves as one of Guil's archons, sure that Guil is good.

title: Das Buch von der Grabkrieg
summary: A medieval prophecy of the Jyhad's ages.

claims.text: Written in the early Middle Ages in German and an untranslated script like Linear A, it looks like a poor monastery manuscript in a single hand.
Its seven cantos, in verse and prose, each cover one age of the world and its Jyhad; the author claims to live in the fourth.
Whether copies of the Grabkrieg can be found is in question.

versions.text: Beckett hunts it as a lost tome.
The Tremere try to restrict it, but copies circulate in secret and many anarchs follow it.

claims.text: It is studied alongside the notes on Gehenna of Doctor Mortius, a Tremere, and Diabolists read it to learn about the elders they hunt.
